sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Indiana County
sections.html:
Indiana County deeds are recorded at the Register & Recorders Office in the county courthouse, 825 Philadelphia Street, Indiana, PA 15701. The phone is 724-465-3860 and the fax is 724-465-3863. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and closed on county holidays.

One office combines the Recorder of Deeds, the Register of Wills and the Clerk of Orphans' Court. It takes deeds, mortgages, satisfactions and other land documents in person, by mail or by e-recording through CSC or Simplifile. Every sale of an Indiana County house ends with the deed going through this counter or its electronic equivalent.

The office publishes a 13-point recording checklist and says the list may not cover every policy. Reading it before closing prevents a returned package.

  • The acknowledgment date can't come before the date on the document. It must show county, state, date, the name and title of the person appearing, and the notary's signature and expiration date.
  • The municipality, county and state must be stated. For parcels in Blacklick, Canoe or Young Townships, the school district must be named too.
  • The UPI parcel number must appear on every real estate document.
  • Numerals must match the written amount on deeds and mortgages.
  • Mortgages must cite a book and page or instrument number that refers back to the original.
  • Deeds and mortgages need a certified grantee or mortgagee address, and the Certificate of Residence must be signed.
  • A deed with land in more than one municipality must state the percentage split of transfer taxes.
  • When several documents make up one transaction, mark the order of recording, for example deed first and then mortgage. Re-recording costs from the wrong order fall on whoever submitted them.

The office doesn't currently accept e-notarizations. An e-recording that makes staff print extra pages, such as a trust copy filed with a deed or the original deed attached to a corrective one, must be sent on paper or it is rejected. A returned document carries a $5 rejection fee.

A deed or mortgage is $91.75 on the document listing the office posted for November 1, 2025, which raised its JCS document fees by $1. Call to confirm the current figure. The fee schedule effective December 1, 2025 sits on the Register & Recorders page.

Add $1 to the total if a stamped, self-addressed return envelope is not included. The office also runs an online fee calculator on its page. Call for a firm figure before sending money.

Indiana County asks for three separate checks made out to Recorder of Deeds, each for an exact amount: one for recording fees, one for the 1% municipal transfer tax and one for the state transfer tax. The printed fee sheet says the same thing by asking for two additional checks on a deed with transfer tax, one for 1% local and one for 1% state.

The deed must either come with a Statement of Value or state its exemption, for example a transfer between family members. One Statement of Value counts as a page of the document, and a second completed copy goes to the Department of Revenue.

The 1% state rate applies to the value of the real estate, and grantor and grantee are both liable. Exemptions cover certain family transfers, transfers to government units and property that passes by will or intestate succession.

The Register & Recorders Office warns that scammers have tried to sell property in the county. It urges owners to sign up for its free Property Alert, which notifies them of fraudulent recordings. It also advises watching for drivers who collect information from vacant properties while claiming to work for utility companies.

A second warning covers text messages saying delinquent taxes must be paid or a property will be sold. The county calls these fraudulent. The tax claim office doesn't text or call owners, and all its notices are written and mailed. Questions go to 724-465-3810.

If you've left a house empty while preparing to list, the alert lets you see every document recorded against the parcel.

The Register of Wills asks anyone opening an estate to make an appointment first, by emailing the office to calculate costs and receive forms. For probate the office wants a copy of the petition, the death certificate, the will and any renunciations, plus the number of short certificates desired, so it can quote a total.

  • Inheritance tax payments can be mailed, and the postmark date counts as the payment date.
  • Short certificates are the papers a bank asks for.
  • The same courthouse office records the deed that follows, so heirs can finish both steps in Indiana.

The county won't change a deed once it is recorded, so any correction to a name needs a new, corrective deed. The posted fee for a corrective deed is $91.75, the same as a regular deed, and one that needs a copy of the original attached must be filed on paper if it is e-recorded.

Heirs who plan to sell should phone 724-465-3860 first, since probate here runs by appointment.

sections.h2: From closing table to recorded deed
sections.html:
Here is how a typical sale moves through the courthouse. The deed is signed and notarized at closing. The closing agent adds the UPI parcel number, checks that numerals match the written amount, and prepares the Statement of Value or the exemption language. If a mortgage is part of the deal, the order of recording is marked on each document.

Next come the three checks and, if you want the recorded original back, a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. The package goes to the courthouse, or the title company e-records it through CSC or Simplifile. Staff review it against the checklist. If everything fits, the deed is recorded and indexed. If not, it is returned with the $5 rejection fee, and the fix and resubmission fall to whoever sent it.

As the seller, you can ask your closing agent which route they use and when the package will arrive. A paper deed that is mailed takes longer than an e-recorded one.

Indiana County has an estimated 82,878 residents as of July 2025, nearly flat from the April 2020 base. The median owner-occupied value is $152,800 and the owner-occupied rate is 72.1% for 2020 to 2024. Monthly owner costs are $1,266 with a mortgage and $540 without, and median gross rent is $800.

A farm or acreage sale here may involve more than one parcel, and each parcel needs its own UPI number on the deed.

faqs.a: Yes, through CSC and Simplifile. The office doesn't currently accept e-notarizations, and an e-recording that needs extra pages printed must be submitted on paper.

faqs.q: What is the rejection fee in Indiana County?
faqs.a: A returned document carries a $5 rejection fee. Checking the recording checklist first avoids it.

faqs.q: Which Indiana County townships need a school district on the deed?
faqs.a: Blacklick, Canoe and Young Townships. The school district must be stated for parcels in those townships.

faqs.q: How many checks does Indiana County want for a deed with transfer tax?
faqs.a: Three, each payable to Recorder of Deeds: one for recording fees, one for the 1% municipal transfer tax and one for the state transfer tax.

faqs.q: How do I confirm the current deed fee in Indiana County?
faqs.a: Call 724-465-3860 or use the fee calculator on the county page. The November 2025 listing shows $91.75 for a deed, and the office asks callers to confirm.
